newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-STOJKO REGAINS WORLD TITLE.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-STOJKO REGAINS WORLD TITLE.

text.p: Canadian Elvis Stojko produced his spectacular trademark, a quadruple-triple jump combination, to recapture the world figure skating title as Olympic and European champion Alexei Urmanov withdrew injured on Thursday.
Stojko, 25 this Saturday, beat off American defending champion Todd Eldredge with Russian 17-year-old Alexei Yagudin third.
Urmanov, leader after Wednesday's short programme and title favourite, pulled out with a groin injury after warming up with just the last group of skaters to go.
His withdrawal also meant that, because of a new qualification system for next year's Winter Olympics in Japan, Russia can have only two entries in the men's event instead of three.
His coach, Alexei Mishin, was unapologetic.
"In the former Soviet Union we would fly into the machine guns for the motherland. Now the health of the athlete is more important," he said.

Urmanov's retirement despite three injections during the day into the groin injured in Wednesday's short programme left Stojko with a virtual open door to walk through to the title he won in 1994 and 1995.
He still had Eldredge to contend with, but the 25-year-old American had nothing to match Stojko's dazzling display and fluffed two jumps late in his programme.

There were a couple of scratchy landings in the rest of Stojko's programme to music from the Movie "Dragonheart", but an Italian judge gave him a perfect 6.0 for technique and the other judges awarded him 5.9.

He had one score of 5.9 for artistry, six of 5.8 and two of 5.6 and won the free skating on the cards of eight of the nine judges to take first place after both totalled 3.0 factored placements based on positions in the short and long programmes.
"I came here wanting to skate two clean programmes and so I'm happy with that," Stojko said. "The result is a bonus."
Stojko first did the quadruple toe loop-triple toe loop combination when he won the Champions Series final in Hamilton, Ontario, early this month.
After his fourth place finish in the short programme, he knew he needed to produce the combination again - and he did.
Eldredge aimed for eight triples and did the first seven - then came unstuck. His eighth, a triple axel, became a single and he was undecided on a later double axel and fell.

"I didn't give myself enough time on the triple axel because I knew I'd missed it in the qualifying. Then I thought I might try it again instead of the double, but it felt weird going in and I knew it had no chance," he said.
Yagudin was delighted with third place because he has had leg injuries recently and was poor in the qualifying round last Sunday.
"I had only three practices before the world championships and I was not ready to skate well. But I felt better yesterday," he said.
Viacheslav Zagorodniuk of Ukraine came fourth as he and Yagudin both made uncharacteristic jumping errors.

Earlier on Friday, Russians Oksana Gritschuk and Evgeny Platov strengthened their lead in the ice dance by winning the tango, with team mates Anjelika Krylova and Oleg Ovsiannikov remaining second and Canadians Shae-Lynn Bourne and Victor Kraatz third.
